source.note: Every entry was authored against the scanned Relations.lean declaration; identifiers are computed from the scanner, not from a second declaration list.

dispositionVocabulary.description: Already represented by an R1 pilot certificate or by a direct parent of one; reuse the pilot certificate.
Direct relation row that still needs a typed certificate before it can become an audit record.
Supporting lemma consumed by a certificate or composition; not itself a standalone relation certificate.
Intra-theory A1/A2/A3 adjudication or boundary; a legal audit record but never one of the 136 cross-theory pairs.
Shape resemblance, non-relation, or contrast; must not be flattened into a direct certified edge.
Machine-checkable shape or boundary note used as metadata; no relation certificate and no edge.
Scoped, one-sided, or transitive registration documenting how a theory sits on the graph.
Associated only with an undelivered candidate relation; no certificate exists and the candidate remains unresolved.

relationRoleVocabulary.description: Two delivered definitions with the same body.
Cross-theory implication in one direction only.
Equivalence under an explicit modelling premise.
Intermediate lemma consumed by a composition.
Composition stated at the modelling level, not by a typed parent.
Supporting fact with no direct relational content.
Bridge between two readings inside one theory.
Adjudication whose endpoints are one theory.
Verdict row of an A1/A2/A3 adjudication.
Boundary or observable row of an adjudication.
Shared functional form or predicate, not an edge.
Checkable difference that separates a look-alike.
Machine note about a shape or boundary, not an edge.
Machine note that pins only one side of a pair.
Tie-back certificate whose pair reading is transitive.

entries.name: kernel_barrier_eq_marcus
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the shared-kernel barrier and the Marcus barrier. The R1 pilot record rec-kernel-pin certifies exactly this identity as a definitionalIdentity, so the migration should reuse the pilot certificate rather than create a second declaration certificate for the same relation.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse pilot record rec-kernel-pin (definitionalIdentity); do not duplicate it.

entries.name: kernel_barrier_eq_hammond
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the shared-kernel barrier and the Hammond forward gap. It is a kernel-to-theory pin, not a direct Marcus-Hammond pair row: a future certificate should be a definitionalIdentity against the shared kernel, and it must not be flattened into a new cross-theory edge.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.barrier; do not treat it as a direct pair row.

entries.name: kernel_barrier_eq_bep
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the shared-kernel barrier and the BEP activation barrier. This is a kernel-to-theory identity, not a direct Marcus-BEP relation; it needs a definitionalIdentity certificate against the shared kernel only.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.barrier; do not infer a pair edge.

entries.name: kernel_reverseBarrier_eq_hammond
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the kernel reverse barrier and the Hammond reverse gap. The row is a kernel-to-Hammond regression pin, not a cross-theory relation between two independent predicates.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.reverseBarrier.

entries.name: kernel_tsCoord_eq_hammond
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the kernel transition-state coordinate and the Hammond coordinate. It is the shared definitional object behind the Marcus-Hammond edge and should remain a kernel pin rather than be counted as a separate direct relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.tsCoord.

entries.name: kernel_transfer_eq_bep
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the kernel transfer coefficient and the BEP coefficient. It is a shared-kernel identity; the legacy Marcus-BEP edge also cites the non-definitional equivalence transfer_eq_tsCoord_bridge, which must not be conflated with this pin.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.transfer.

entries.name: kernel_reactantSurface_eq_hammond
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the kernel reactant surface and the Hammond surface. This is a kernel-to-theory regression certificate, not a cross-theory pair relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.reactantSurface.

entries.name: kernel_productSurface_eq_hammond
entries.rationale: Definitional rfl pin between the kernel product surface and the Hammond product surface. It records shared definitions, not a new cross-theory relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.productSurface.

entries.name: transfer_eq_tsCoord_bridge
entries.rationale: Genuine non-definitional equivalence between the BEP transfer coefficient and the Hammond transition-state coordinate under the explicit premise lam != 0. This is a direct Hammond-BEP relation and needs a typed equivalence certificate; it is not a definitional identity.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate with the lam != 0 premise.

entries.name: secSlope_eq_lefflerSecant
entries.rationale: Genuine equivalence between the BEP observable secant slope and the Hammond Leffler secant. The bodies differ in sign convention and pair indexing, so this is a theorem-level equivalence, not an rfl identity; it is a direct Hammond-BEP relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate; do not close it by rfl.

entries.name: epBounds_iff_no_inverted_direction
entries.rationale: Headline equivalence: the Evans-Polanyi bounds hold exactly when neither direction lies in the Marcus inverted region. The R1 pilot uses this theorem as the parent certificate epBoundsNoInvertedEquivalence of rec-composition, so the migration should reuse the pilot certificate rather than duplicate the relation.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse the R1 parent certificate epBoundsNoInvertedEquivalence used by rec-composition.

entries.name: tsCoord_lt_zero_iff_inverted
entries.rationale: Equivalence between the transition state leaving the reactant side and the Marcus inverted region. This is a genuine Marcus-Hammond relation with a positive-curvature premise; it needs a typed equivalence certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate with the lam > 0 premise.

entries.name: lefflerSecant_neg_iff_inverted
entries.rationale: Equivalence between a negative Leffler secant and the Marcus inverted region at the midpoint. It is a theorem-level Marcus-Hammond relation, not a definitional identity, and it needs a typed equivalence certificate with its distinct-point premise.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate with lam > 0 and x1 != x2.

entries.name: hammondZoneQ_beyondReactant_iff_inverted
entries.rationale: Rational-side agreement between the Hammond deep-exergonic classifier and the Marcus rational inverted-region classifier. It is a cross-theory equivalence over the rationals and needs a typed certificate; it is not the same statement as the real-valued rows.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate over Q with lam > 0.

entries.name: epBounds_of_reactionRegion
entries.rationale: One-way entailment from Hammonds conformance region to the Evans-Polanyi bounds. The R1 pilot record rec-hammond-bep certifies exactly this implication, so the migration should reuse it; the converse is not claimed.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse pilot record rec-hammond-bep (implication).

entries.name: epBounds_of_marcus_normal
entries.rationale: One-way entailment from the Marcus normal region plus reverse thermoneutrality to the Evans-Polanyi bounds. The R1 pilot uses this row as the parent certificate marcusNormalImplication of rec-composition, so the migration should reuse that certificate and keep the one-way direction.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse the R1 parent certificate marcusNormalImplication used by rec-composition.

entries.name: hammondDescriptor_of_epConformsOnWindow
entries.rationale: New one-way entailment from BEP window conformance to the structural Hammond descriptor. The proof consumes only the positivity conjunct of EPConformsOnWindow, so the tolerance bound is not load-bearing; a typed implication certificate should record that one-way reading and must not claim the converse.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed implication certificate and document that only the positivity conjunct is consumed.

entries.name: hammond_descriptor_of_inner
entries.rationale: Definitional-reuse support: the Marcus inner-sphere reorganization energy yields the Hammond descriptor directly. It is an intermediate lemma feeding the Marcus-Hammond composition, not a standalone cross-theory relation certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as support for the Marcus-Hammond composition; do not register as a standalone relation.

entries.name: hammond_descriptor_of_microscopic
entries.rationale: Microscopic-premise support: the Pekar and geometric premises on the Marcus outer-sphere term make the total reorganization energy positive and hence the Hammond descriptor holds. This is a support lemma for the Marcus-Hammond edge, not a second edge certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as support for the Marcus-Hammond composition.

entries.name: hammond_descriptor_of_nonoverlap
entries.rationale: Stretch-form support: the geometric premise is derived from non-overlapping spheres, still yielding the Hammond descriptor. It is a variant support lemma for the same Marcus-Hammond composition.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as support; do not duplicate the Marcus-Hammond certificate.

entries.name: exists_reactionRegion_of_microscopic
entries.rationale: Non-vacuity support: the Marcus microscopic premises produce an actual Hammond reaction region. This supports the Hammond edge by exhibiting a witness, but it is not itself a relation certificate between two predicates.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as a non-vacuity/support lemma.

entries.name: bep_eact_eq_marcus_barrier
entries.rationale: Ledger alias: the BEP activation barrier is the delivered Marcus barrier. Both definitions have the same body, so this is a definitionalIdentity candidate; it is a different row from the R1 kernel pin, which pins Kernel.barrier rather than BEP.eact.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate for BEP.eact and Marcus.barrier; do not conflate it with the kernel pin.

entries.name: bep_rate_eq_exp_neg_eact
entries.rationale: Rate rewriting: the delivered Marcus rate written through the BEP activation barrier. Both sides are the same term after unfolding the two definitions, so a definitionalIdentity certificate is appropriate; it is not a new theorem-level edge.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate for the rate rewriting.

entries.name: hammond_barrier_eq_gapReactant
entries.rationale: Theory-level alias: the Marcus barrier is literally the Hammond forward gap. It is a definitional alias certificate, not an independent equivalence, and it should be recorded as a definitionalIdentity rather than an rfl-free edge.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate for the Marcus-Hammond barrier alias.

entries.name: marcus_rat_zoneQ_inverted_iff
entries.rationale: Rational-side bridge inside the Marcus theory: the rational inverted-region decision connects to the real inequality after the delivered transfer rewrites. It supports the Marcus classifier and is intra-theory, so it is not one of the 136 cross-theory pairs and should not be registered as an edge.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as intra-theory support; exclude from the 136-pair numerator.

entries.name: hammond_trend_exact_bep_law_inexact
entries.rationale: Exactness contrast: in one model the Hammond structural trend is exactly affine while the BEP line law is exactly false on every non-degenerate interval. The legacy Hammond-BEP edge cites this row, but it is a shape/difference theorem, not a direct relation between the two predicates; it must not be flattened into a certified edge.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike/difference row; do not create a Hammond-BEP edge certificate from it.

entries.name: hammond_sharp_iff_marcus_sharp
entries.rationale: Co-extensiveness of the Hammond structural descriptor and the Marcus rate descriptor, proved by composing the two delivered sharp characterizations. It is a genuine cross-theory equivalence and needs a typed equivalence certificate; it is not a definitional identity and its content is the co-extensiveness itself.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate; keep the composition provenance visible.

entries.name: rate_predicate_satisfiable_without_positive_curvature
entries.rationale: Counterexample row: the Marcus rate predicate alone is satisfiable with negative curvature while the Hammond structural descriptor fails. This is an adjudication-style contrast showing the predicates are not equally strong; it is not a direct relation certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a non-relation/contrast row; do not create an edge certificate.

entries.name: kernel_marcusIC
entries.rationale: Kernel pin: the Kasha internal-conversion rate is the kernel barrier inside the Marcus rate law. It is a definitionalIdentity candidate and the definitional core of the Kasha-Marcus edge, not a separate theorem-level relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against the kernel barrier.

entries.name: kashaWithin_one_marcus
entries.rationale: Conditional equivalence under the declared hic modelling premise: Kasha conformance is exactly the explicit window condition on the squared energy gap. The R1 pilot certifies exactly this as rec-kasha-marcus, so it must be reused as a conditional equivalence and must not be relabelled as a composition.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse pilot record rec-kasha-marcus (conditional equivalence under hic).

entries.name: not_kashaWithin_of_gap_far
entries.rationale: One-way consequence of the conditional Kasha-Marcus equivalence: a gap outside the window violates the tolerance. It is a supporting consequence for the window reading, not a standalone certificate and not an anti-Kasha edge.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as support for the conditional Kasha-Marcus certificate.

entries.name: kashaWindow_halfWidth
entries.rationale: Alternate half-width presentation of the same Kasha-Marcus window condition. It is a support/alternative-form lemma, not a new pair relation, and it should not be counted as a second certificate for the pair.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as an alternative-form support lemma.

entries.name: marcusIC_pos
entries.rationale: Positivity of the Marcus-form internal-conversion rate whenever the pre-exponential factor is positive. It is a support fact for the Kasha-Marcus reading, not a relation certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as a positivity support fact.

entries.name: linearVolcano_eq_bepTangent
entries.rationale: Identity: the Sabatier linear volcano is the maximum of the two BEP tangent lines at thermoneutrality. It is a delivered composition result and needs a typed certificate; it is not a definitional rfl identity.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition/equivalence certificate for the Sabatier-BEP volcano identity.

entries.name: bepLine_le_eact
entries.rationale: Pointwise tangent-below-parabola inequality, the geometric reading of the BEP defect law. It is a component of the Sabatier-BEP composition, not a standalone pair certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as a composition component.

entries.name: linearVolcano_le_parabolic
entries.rationale: Pointwise lower bound of the linear volcano by the two-parabola volcano: the linear model underestimates the barrier away from the apex. This is a composition result and needs a typed order/implication certificate, not an edge label alone.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed pointwise-order certificate.

entries.name: parabolic_descriptor
entries.rationale: The Sabatier volcano descriptor holds in the two-parabola model with no BEP linearization. This is a composition certificate showing the descriptor survives the exact model; it needs a typed certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the descriptor.

entries.name: apexPar_self
entries.rationale: A symmetric two-parabola cycle has its apex at the thermoneutral descriptor value. It is a supporting component of the apex comparison, not a standalone relation certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as a composition component.

entries.name: linearVolcano_apex_exact
entries.rationale: At a symmetric cycles apex the tangent-line model and the parabola model agree exactly. This is a composition result about the apex and needs a typed certificate; it does not license a general equivalence of the two models.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed apex-composition certificate.

entries.name: marcus_rate_eq_activity
entries.rationale: C1: the Marcus rate is the Sabatier activity functional applied to the kernel barrier, scaled by the pre-exponential factor. This is a shared functional form (C1 is a certificate of coincidence, not an edge); the Marcus-Sabatier pair is a look-alike, so the row must not be flattened into a direct edge certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike shared-form row; do not create a Marcus-Sabatier edge.

entries.name: marcusRate_antiVolcanoDescriptor
entries.rationale: C2: the Marcus rate satisfies the very same Sabatier anti-volcano predicate, with lam as its unique maximizer. This is a shared-predicate look-alike, not a direct relation between the two theories; the uniqueness half is new mathematics but does not create an edge.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike shared-predicate row.

entries.name: apexBarrier_reference_nonzero
entries.rationale: C3a: the Sabatier reference pass height is 1/2, so a volcano pass is not a barrierless point. It is a supporting component of the C3 contrast, not a cross-theory relation by itself.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as a supporting component of the look-alike contrast.

entries.name: optimal_barrier_height_contrast
entries.rationale: C3b: the Marcus optimal barrier is identically zero while the Sabatier reference pass is 1/2. This side-by-side contrast is the checkable content of look-alike but different and is not a direct edge.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike contrast row.

entries.name: marcus_secant_at_optimum
entries.rationale: C4: the Marcus one-sided secant at the optimum is h/(4*lam), hence vanishes with the step, while the Sabatier volcano legs have step-independent secant slopes. This kink-versus-smooth-optimum contrast is a non-relation, not an edge.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike contrast row.

entries.name: sabatier_apex_moves_with_offsets
entries.rationale: C5a: the Sabatier apex moves when only the offsets change with the slopes held fixed. It is a component of the C5 contrast between the two optima, not a cross-theory relation on its own.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike contrast component.

entries.name: marcus_optimum_fixed_by_curvature
entries.rationale: C5b: the Marcus optimal position is fixed by the curvature alone, whereas C5a shows the Sabatier apex responding to offsets. This is the contrast half of the look-alike pair and must not become an edge certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Register as a look-alike contrast row.

entries.name: symmetryFactor_tsCoordZero_eq_kernel
entries.rationale: A1 tie-back certificate: at equal curvature the SymmetryFactor thermoneutral coordinate is the kernel transition-state coordinate. No row names Marcus directly; the Marcus-SymmetryFactor legacy edge is transitive through the shared kernel, so the migration must keep that transitive reading rather than claim a direct row.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed tie-back certificate and record the transitive-via-kernel boundary.

entries.name: symmetryFactor_tsCoordZero_eq_bepTransfer
entries.rationale: A1 tie-back certificate: at equal curvature the SymmetryFactor coordinate is the delivered BEP transfer coefficient at thermoneutrality, extending the E1 chain. The BEP-SymmetryFactor legacy edge is transitive through the kernel/E1 chain, not a direct two-theory row.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed tie-back certificate and record the transitive boundary.

entries.name: symmetryFactor_betaHalf_iff
entries.rationale: A1 verdict: the beta = 1/2 reading holds exactly when the two force constants agree. The R1 pilot certifies this as the intra-theory equivalence rec-a1; it is not one of the 136 cross-theory pairs and must not be counted as an edge.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse pilot record rec-a1 (intra-theory equivalence).

entries.name: symmetryFactor_conflation_falsified_and_holds_in_kernel
entries.rationale: A1 falsification-and-persistence verdict inside SymmetryFactor: the conflated reading is refuted at an unequal pair and holds throughout the equal-curvature family. It is an intra-theory adjudication record, not a cross-theory pair, and it adds no new pair coverage.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as an intra-theory adjudication record; exclude from the 136-pair numerator.
entries.notes: Related to pilot record rec-a1, which certifies the equivalence half only.

entries.name: eg_barrier_eq_kernel
entries.rationale: Batch definitional pin: the EnergyGapLaw barrier is the kernel barrier. It is a kernel-to-theory rfl pin, not a direct EnergyGapLaw-Marcus relation; a definitionalIdentity certificate is required.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.barrier.

entries.name: eg_rate_eq_marcus
entries.rationale: Batch definitional pin: the EnergyGapLaw rate is the Marcus rate. This is a direct EnergyGapLaw-Marcus definitional identity and needs a typed certificate; it is not a theorem-level equivalence.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate for the EnergyGapLaw-Marcus rate.

entries.name: eg_invertedGap_iff_marcus
entries.rationale: Batch equivalence: the EnergyGapLaw inverted-gap predicate is the Marcus inverted region. It is a propositional equivalence, not a definitional identity, and it needs a typed equivalence certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate for the inverted-gap predicate.

entries.name: ss_s0Surface_eq_kernel
entries.rationale: Batch definitional pin: the StokesShift ground surface is the kernel reactant surface. It is a kernel-to-theory rfl pin, not a direct cross-theory pair relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.reactantSurface.

entries.name: ss_s1Surface_eq_kernel
entries.rationale: Batch definitional pin: the StokesShift excited surface is the kernel product surface. It is a kernel-to-theory rfl pin and should remain a definitional certificate rather than an edge.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.productSurface.

entries.name: icvscic_barrier_eq_kernel
entries.rationale: Batch definitional pin: the ICvsISC Franck-Condon barrier is the kernel barrier. It is a kernel-to-theory rfl pin, not a direct two-theory relation.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate against PhotoLean.Kernel.barrier.

entries.name: icvscic_icRate_eq_marcus
entries.rationale: Batch definitional pin: the ICvsISC internal-conversion rate is the Marcus rate. This is a direct Marcus-ICvsISC definitional identity and needs a typed certificate; it must not be conflated with the separate EnergyGapLaw rate identity.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate for the Marcus-ICvsISC rate.

entries.name: kv_d2_verdict
entries.rationale: A2 four-part adjudication of Kasha rule against Vavilov behavior: pointwise independence both ways, the closed-form coincidence boundary, and the lossless separation. It is an intra-theory adjudication record, not one of the 136 cross-theory pairs; the R1 refutation record overlaps its first conjunct but does not certify the whole verdict.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as an intra-theory adjudication record; do not count it as a Kasha-KashaVavilov pair edge.
entries.notes: The R1 record rec-kasha-vavilov overlaps the first refutation conjunct only.

entries.name: kv_antiKasha_boundary
entries.rationale: A2 boundary: under RateData, a violation of Kasha rule is always an observable anti-Kasha emission. It is an intra-theory boundary result, not a cross-theory pair relation.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as an intra-theory adjudication boundary.

entries.name: sv_d1_verdict
entries.rationale: A3 three-part adjudication inside SternVolmer: both plots are linear, the intensity observation map is non-injective, and lifetime tracking identifies the mechanism. It is an intra-theory adjudication; the R1 pilot certifies the intensity, joint-distinguishability and decoder parts, but the full verdict remains intra-theory.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as an intra-theory adjudication record; exclude from the 136-pair numerator.
entries.notes: Overlaps pilot records rec-sv-intensity, rec-sv-joint and rec-sv-decoder but is broader.

entries.name: sv_identifiability_boundary
entries.rationale: A3 identifiability boundary: lifetime tracking holds iff the mechanism is dynamic, with 0 < Ka load-bearing. The R1 decoder certificate rec-sv-decoder derives from the same theory theorem, so the migration should reuse the pilot certificate; this is intra-theory, not a 136 pair.
entries.migrationAction: Reuse pilot record rec-sv-decoder (intra-theory decoder).

entries.name: kasha_radBranch_eq_yieldOf
entries.rationale: Composition: the Kasha radiative branch is the two-channel quantum yield. It is a delivered composition result and needs a typed certificate; it is not a definitional identity despite the algebraic unfolding.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the Kasha-QuantumYield link.

entries.name: sv_quench_dilutes_yield
entries.rationale: Composition: dynamic quenching is exactly quantum-yield dilution. The theorem consumes both the SternVolmer ratio and the QuantumYield functional, so it is a genuine composition and needs a typed certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the SternVolmer-QuantumYield link.

entries.name: phiF_eq_yieldOf
entries.rationale: Composition: the FluorPhos fluorescence yield is the three-channel quantum yield. It is a typed composition candidate, not a definitional alias of a shared definition.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the FluorPhos-QuantumYield link.

entries.name: phiP_eq_yieldOf_cascade
entries.rationale: Composition: the FluorPhos phosphorescence yield is a cascade product of two quantum yields. It consumes the QuantumYield layer twice and is a genuine composition, not an edge label alone.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the phosphorescence cascade.

entries.name: einstein_yield_via_qy
entries.rationale: Composition: the two-channel fluorescence yield with radiative rate A is the Einstein-side anchor of the radiative channel. It is a typed composition candidate between Einstein and QuantumYield.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the Einstein-QuantumYield anchor.

entries.name: fretEff6_eq_one_sub_yieldOf
entries.rationale: Composition: the FRET efficiency is one minus the donor yield of the channel-added model. It is a genuine composition consuming Forster and QuantumYield, not a definitional identity.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the Forster-QuantumYield link.

entries.name: marcusIC_strictAnti_on_inverted_gaps
entries.rationale: Monotonicity of the Kasha internal-conversion rate in the Marcus inverted gap. It supports the Kasha-Marcus composition and the EnergyGapLaw rationale, but it consumes no EnergyGapLaw declaration, so the legacy Kasha-EnergyGapLaw edge is one-sided and must not be flattened into a K-EGL certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as support; do not create an EnergyGapLaw-Kasha certificate from this row.

entries.name: egBarrier_zero_iff_emEnergy_zero
entries.rationale: Equivalence: the EnergyGapLaw barrier vanishes exactly when the Stokes emission window closes. It is a genuine cross-theory equivalence and needs a typed certificate with the lam != 0 premise.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed equivalence certificate for the emission-window boundary.

entries.name: icvscic_icRate_eq_eg_nrRate
entries.rationale: Definitional pin: the ICvsISC internal-conversion rate is the EnergyGapLaw nonradiative rate. Both bodies coincide after unfolding the barriers, so it is a definitionalIdentity candidate, not a theorem-level equivalence.
entries.migrationAction: Add a definitionalIdentity certificate for the ICvsISC-EnergyGapLaw rate.

entries.name: fpRatio_invariant_under_quench
entries.rationale: Quench invariance of the fluorescence/phosphorescence ratio. The SternVolmer side is encoded as the added rate kq*q rather than through a SternVolmer declaration, so this is a model-level composition; a typed certificate needs an explicit translation/bridge before it can be a composition record.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed certificate only after declaring the kq*q translation; do not claim a typed parent composition yet.

entries.name: fretEff6_inv_eq_one_plus
entries.rationale: FO/SV shape note: the inverse FRET efficiency is a 1 + control law with the sixth-power distance control. Section 16 registers this as a shape with machine content, not an edge; it is metadata only and must not become a SternVolmer-Forster edge certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as metadata; do not create a SternVolmer-Forster edge.

entries.name: eg_boundary_eq_tsCoord_zero
entries.rationale: EGL/Hammond boundary row: the kernel transition-state coordinate vanishes exactly at lam = x. The legacy census cites this as an EnergyGapLaw-Hammond edge, but the row is a kernel boundary identity, not a direct relation between EnergyGapLaw and Hammond predicates; keep it as scoped documentation.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as scoped boundary documentation; do not create a direct EnergyGapLaw-Hammond certificate.

entries.name: raci_qy_eq_yieldOf_two_channel
entries.rationale: Composition certificate: the RACI quantum yield is the two-channel QuantumYield. It consumes the QuantumYield layer and is a genuine composition, not a definitional alias.
entries.migrationAction: Add a typed composition certificate for the RACI-QuantumYield link.

entries.name: qy_two_channel_strictAnti_of_nr_lt
entries.rationale: Supporting row: the RACI enhancement is the two-channel strict-antitone-in-knr reading of the QuantumYield layer. It is a composition component/support lemma, not a standalone pair certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Retain as a composition component.

entries.name: log_barrierRate_eq
entries.rationale: RACI barrier-rate log is affine in B with slope -beta. This is a one-sided machine note on the RACI side: no EnergyGapLaw declaration is consumed, so the EnergyGapLaw-RACI legacy edge is documentation of a shape, not a typed composition.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as scoped one-sided documentation; do not create a typed EnergyGapLaw-RACI composition.

entries.name: icvsisc_barrier_zero_at_crossing
entries.rationale: At a conical intersection the ICvsISC Franck-Condon barrier vanishes. The row pins only the ICvsISC side; the RACI side is not consumed, so the RACI-ICvsISC legacy edge is a one-sided machine note, not a composition certificate.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as scoped one-sided documentation; do not create a typed RACI-ICvsISC composition.

entries.name: kernel_surfaces_cross_at_tsCoord
entries.rationale: RACI/Marcus look-alike machine note: the classical two-parabola model has a real surface crossing at the transition-state coordinate, while the RACI conical intersection is a two-condition degeneracy. The legacy section-17 register counts the pair as an absence/look-alike; keep this as metadata only.
entries.migrationAction: Keep as metadata; do not create a Marcus-RACI edge.
